Iqbal Khan vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 19 September, 2023
 High Court Of Chhattisgarh, Bilaspur
 Order Sheet
I.A. No. 1 of 2022

In Re :
 Cra No. 1963 of 2022
 1.

Iqbal Khan son of Gulbir Khan, aged about 32 years, resident of
 Village - Urla Ramsagar Para, at present Kailash Nagar, Dhamdha Naka,
 Police Station- Mohan Nagr, District - Durg (C.G.)
 2. Hansraj Sahu, son of Manrakhan Sahu, aged about 42 years, resident
 of Ramsagar Para, Urla, Bhilai-3, District - Durg (C.G.)
 ---- Appellants
 (In jail)
 Versus
 State of Chhattisgarh, through the Station House Officer, Police Station-
 Purani Bhilai, District Durg (C.G.)
 ---- Respondent
(Cause-title taken from Case Information System) 19/09/2023

By the impugned judgment of
conviction and order of sentence dated 19.10.2022, learned Additional Sessions Judge (F.T.C.),
District Durg in Sessions Trial No. 42 of 2016, has convicted and sentenced the appellants in
following manner :-
Conviction Sentence Under Section 302 /34 of Ipc For Life imprisonment which means rigorous
imprisonment for the remainder of the natural life of the accused persons and fine of Rs.5,000/-, in
default of payment of fine, to further undergo R.I. for one year, each.

Under Section 376-D of IPC For Life imprisonment which means rigorous imprisonment for the remainder of the natural life of the accused persons and fine of Rs.5,000/-, in default of payment of fine, to further undergo R.I. for one year, each.
Heard Mr. Amit Soni, counsel for the appellants.
Also heard Mr. Avinash Singh, Panel Lawyer appearing for the State/respondent on the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail (IA No. 1 of 2022).

Learned Counsel for the convict/appellants submits that appellants have been falsely implicated in the crime in question, as there is no evidence available on record to connect the appellants with the crime in question.

He submits that the appellants are in jail since 04.12.2015 and the appeal is likely to take a couple of years or even more for its final disposal, hence he prays that the appellants may be enlarged on bail.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent/State while opposing the bail application filed by the appellants would submit that as per case of the prosecution, appellants have sexually abused the victim/prosecutrix two times and thereafter they set her on fire, as a result thereof, she received several burn injuries on her person and succumbed to these injuries during the course of treatment at Burn Unit Ward, District Hospital, Durg.

He further submits the victim/prosecutrix, in her statement recorded under Section 161 of the Cr.P.C., has categorically stated that both the appellants have forcefully sexually abused her two times and, thereafter, with an intention to kill her, they set her on fire, resultantly, she received burn injuries on her person, and, thereafter, one lady has assisted her by giving her Saree and, thereafter, called the Ambulance and sent her for treatment at District Hospital, Durg.

He submits that dying declaration of the deceased was also recorded, in which, she has categorically stated against the accused/appellants, as such, looking to the seriousness of the crime, the appellants are not entitled to be enlarged on bail.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties, having regard to the facts & circumstances of the case,
particularly, considering the statement of the victim /deceased recorded under Section 161 of the Cr.P.C., in which, she has clearly stated that appellants have sexually abused her two times and thereafter they set her on fire with an intention to kill her; further considering the fact that her dying declaration of the victim/deceased (Ex.P-23) was also recorded, in which, she had also categorically stated against the both the appellants, thus, looking to the heinousness of the crime, we deem it appropriate to reject the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail at this stage.
Accordingly, IA No. 1 of 2022 stands disposed of.
It transpires from the record that the matter is ripe for final hearing.
Let the matter be listed for final hearing after eight weeks.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (N.K. Chandravanshi (Ramesh Sinha)
